name: Lucidspark
tagline: Collaborative whiteboards for brainstorming, planning, and workshops

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

verdictSummary: The visible whiteboarding loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Lucidspark earns its keep through interaction polish, collaboration, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a browser-based whiteboarding editor with drag, resize, connect, keyboard shortcuts, autosave, and SVG or PNG export.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
whyPeopleStillPay: Lucidspark: The shapes are easy; customers pay for low-friction editing, reliable exports, collaboration, and a canvas that never fights them.
ongoingBurden: Own geometry, selection behavior, undo, clipboard interoperability, export fidelity, accessibility, and browser performance.

priorArt.name: Excalidraw
priorArt.desc: Open-source diagram canvas with an approachable interaction model.

alternatives.name: AFFiNE
alternatives.desc: Collaborative whiteboards tied to docs, databases, and planning views; broader than Lucidspark, more infrastructure if self-hosted.

alternatives.name: CryptPad
alternatives.desc: Persistent encrypted whiteboards inside a shared drive with permissions and team folders; visually plain, operationally serious.

alternatives.name: Excalidraw
alternatives.desc: Fast multiplayer whiteboards, libraries, links, exports, and workshop-friendly sketching; fewer facilitation widgets, much less account bureaucracy.

alternatives.name: tldraw
alternatives.desc: A frictionless hosted multiplayer canvas for brainstorming and planning; templates and enterprise workshop controls are sparse.

alternatives.name: WBO
alternatives.desc: The basic communal whiteboard that keeps working: persistent rooms, live cursors, free hosting, and almost no workshop theatre.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Lucidspark is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Lucidspark, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: React + TypeScript + Vite + IndexedDB.
Primary job: Build a browser-based whiteboarding editor with drag, resize, connect, keyboard shortcuts, autosave, and SVG or PNG export.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: high-fidelity import and export; presentation and enterprise controls; multiplayer cursors and comments.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
